newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Ahold third qtr net jumps on U.S. buy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ahold third qtr net jumps on U.S. buy.

text.p: Dutch retail group Koninklijke Ahold NV announced sharply higher third quarter net profits on Wednesday, largely due to extra sales after a U.S. acquisition.
It said 1996 full-year net earnings would be significantly higher than last year.

Ahold, which earlier this year bought the Stop & Shop retail chain in the United States for a total $2.9 billion, said net profit jumped to 156.4 million guilders ($91.41 million) from 101.6 million guilders.
Operating profit surged to 307.6 million guilders from 211.0 million guilders, and net earnings per share rose to 0.93 guilders from 0.81 guilders in the same 1995 period.
Third quarter turnover increased to 9.27 billion guilders from 6.94 billion guilders, largely due to the extra sales generated in the United States by Stop & Shop.

Ahold, which owns the biggest Dutch supermarket group Albert Heijn, had previously said that the Stop & Shop acquisition, which was included in Ahold's figures for the first time in the third quarter, would further boost operating and net profit.
"Further growth of earnings per share is expected to be positively influenced by the acquisition of Stop & Shop," Ahold said in a statement on Wednesday.
The profits were bang in line with analysts' forecasts for third third quarter net of between 134 and 170 million guilders.
Ahold will pay a 4.20 guilder dividend on its preferred shares.
In Amsterdam, Ahold stock edged 1.80 guilders lower to 104.50 guilders each. ($1=1.711 Guilder)
